summary: API proxy 5xx surge caused by large header aggregation and keepalive backpressure
description:
Issue summary:
- Starting 2026-03-10 09:10 UTC we observed an elevated 5xx rate on several customer streaming routes for BeaconDocs. Errors were primarily 502/503 from the API proxy with correlated upstream runtime connection resets.

Impact:
- Affected ~120 concurrent streaming sessions for the customer across us-east-1; user-facing timeouts and partial transcript losses. Estimated request failure rate peaked at ~18% for the customer route.

Environment:
- prod | us-east (edge + regional apigw fleet). Customer is on Dedicated capacity with tenant pinned model redwood-open-7b-v1.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Customer opens many long-lived streaming sessions with keepalive enabled and large custom headers (X-Client-Meta payload ~8-12KB aggregated across hop-by-hop headers).
2) Upstream ingress aggregated the header frames while apigw queued incoming frames under a keepalive spike.
3) Under moderate concurrency ramp the proxy reported accept queue growth and began hedged retry behavior, triggering upstream connection resets and 502/503 responses.

Observed logs / metrics snippets:
- apigw.accept_queue_length spike from 20 -> 320 over 3m (us-east apigw-09).
- Proxy log: "header size exceeded soft limit, deferring parse" followed by "upstream reset before headers complete".
- runtime: connection closed by peer; nvml/gpu not OOMing. No model load errors.
- tcp traces show half-close sequences and retransmits between apigw and regional ingress.

Hypothesis:
- A combination of unusually large per-connection headers (customer metadata) plus many long-lived streaming keepalives caused head-of-line blocking in apigw's parser thread and accept queue. Parser backpressure amplified request latency and triggered hedged retries that overwhelmed a subset of ephemeral upstream workers, resulting in connection resets and 5xx spikes.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced locally against a staging apigw instance by replaying BeaconDocs traffic (large headers + 150 concurrent streams). Parser thread utilization went to 95% and accept queue grew similarly.
- Heap and CPU on serving-runtime instances stable; GPU metrics normal.
- Auth service reported intermittent increases in header-parsing latency tied to JWT enrichment hooks (customer uses custom auth headers).
- Noted correlation with a recent auth-hook rollout (rolled 2026-03-09) that introduced extra header fields.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Applied ingress-level rate limit for BeaconDocs streaming route to cap new session accepts at 40 r/s while investigation continued.
- Enabled temporary header-size rejection at apigw (soft limit lowered to 6KB) for the tenant to prevent oversized metadata from entering the parse pipeline.
- Whitelisted responses restore path to avoid impacting existing long-lived sessions.

Workaround for customer:
- Advised BeaconDocs to reduce X-Client-Meta header size and disable per-message metadata enrichment temporarily. They implemented a partial client-side fix (metadata compression) which reduced header sizes by ~60%.

Next steps / proposed fixes:
1) Engineering to implement a non-blocking header parser for apigw to avoid single-thread HL blocking (PR under review).
2) Add backpressure metrics and early-dropping counters per-tenant to surface header-aggregation events.
3) Revert the auth-hook enrichment rollout until header size and parsing improvements are in place.
4) Postmortem and runbook update to include "large header aggregation" scenario and customer guidance.

Customer communication plan:
- Notified BeaconDocs CS lead (Emily R.) at 2026-03-10 10:20 UTC with mitigation steps. Follow-up scheduled 2026-03-12.

2026-03-10 10:40 UTC - Diego Morales (SRE): Confirmed accept queue spike on apigw-09 and applied tenant-level rate cap. Noted auth-hook rollout correlation.
2026-03-10 11:05 UTC - SRE (Arun Gupta): Replayed BeaconDocs traffic in staging. Reproduced parser thread saturation. Filed runtime PR to add non-blocking header parsing (see related PR).
2026-03-10 11:30 UTC - Customer (Emily R., BeaconDocs): Implemented client-side metadata compression; reported immediate reduction in failure rate to ~3%.
2026-03-11 09:00 UTC - Diego Morales: Deployed temporary apigw soft-limit config. Monitoring for secondary regressions.
2026-03-12 14:20 UTC - Priya Patel: Customer confirmed service largely restored. Leaving in-progress while engineering completes parser patch and runbook updates.
resolution_notes: Mitigation: tenant rate cap + apigw soft header-size limit + customer compressed headers. Engineering patch for non-blocking header parse in review (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/4321). Plan to fully restore default limits after deploy and postmortem. Follow-up: update runbook and add per-tenant header-aggregation alerts.
next_steps: Merge gateway non-blocking-header-parse PR and canary in us-east small fleet
Revert auth-hook enrichment rollout after validating header parsing improvements
Create postmortem and customer-facing summary by 2026-03-15
